solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Record for posterity the Spanish University's opening with German backing

indicators.note: backing means the whole string of pieces is read from its end to its start

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article
an opening is a gap or space
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A historian archives something from a Spanish university's launch, with German sponsorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reverses everything that comes before it; mit is a German word the solver must know.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed container of objects buried to be opened by future generations is a record kept for posterity.

clue.text: Bound to display confidence in audio version

indicators.note: an audio version is something heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: confidence in someone is trust

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to sound confident when making a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tied up tightly with rope is to be bound hand and foot, past participle for past participle.

clue.text: Household servants get on

parts.note: men can mean male servants or retainers
to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: The domestic staff are growing old, or perhaps getting along.
explanation.definitionFit: A ménage is a domestic establishment, the people living together under one roof.

clue.text: Say I should enter sort of educational establishment

indicators.note: should enter signals that one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to collate is to sort papers into order
EG (for example) is the usual crossword rendering of say

explanation.surface: Someone claims they ought to be admitted to a particular kind of school.
explanation.definitionFit: Collegiate is the adjective relating to a college, a kind of place of learning.

clue.text: Ring jewel Queen removed

indicators.note: removed means the letter for the queen is taken out of the gem

parts.note: a pearl is a jewel
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A ring's precious stone was taken off by the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a ringing of bells, so the noun ring is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Shocked prude, excessively upset internally, pulled out

indicators.note: internally means one piece sits inside the other
shocked suggests the letters of the word prude are jolted into a new order
upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: too means excessively

explanation.surface: A prudish person, terribly shocked, storms out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocked' rearranges prude into UPRED, which is split open by the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants pulled out of the ground roots and all have been uprooted.

clue.text: Shops bearing nameless sign set up, inviting first of punters in

indicators.note: in means the punters' initial goes inside the other letters
set up in a down clue means raised, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: a person's air is their bearing or manner

indicators.note: nameless means the letter for name is dropped

parts.note: an omen is a sign

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of punters

explanation.surface: Shops put up a sign with no name, hoping to draw in customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns the pair upside down, giving EMORIA; 'inviting ... in' then admits the punters' initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large store or place of trade.

clue.text: Vase stored in pan for the day

indicators.note: stored in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: pan is slang for the face, as is dial
an urn is a kind of vase

explanation.surface: A vase is kept in a cooking pot just for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal describes what lasts or happens during the daytime, or recurs daily.

clue.text: A Communist crime suppressed by quiet heroism

indicators.note: suppressed by means held down inside another piece

parts.note: dry in the sense of understated or restrained, as in dry wit
red is the traditional label for a communist
evil is wrongdoing or a crime

explanation.surface: A communist's crime is hushed up by quiet heroism.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless boldness is a kind of heroism, the quality of acting fearlessly.

clue.text: Roman general in a thrilling production on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a gripping show is a gripper

explanation.surface: A Roman general features in an exciting radio drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa was Augustus's leading commander, victor at Actium.

clue.text: Youthful period sadly ceased once around 50

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go about the numeral
sadly signals the words ceased once are jumbled

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A happy youth sadly came to an end some time around the age of fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: The teenage years between childhood and adulthood are a youthful period of life.

clue.text: Left without hope of change

definitions.meaning: having quit a job, stepped down from a post
accepting that something cannot be altered

explanation.walkthrough: One reading is a past tense verb, the other an adjective of glum acceptance.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting a post is stepping down from it; being reconciled to fate means accepting things will not improve.

clue.text: Judge confronting the Telegraph's refusal to identify writer?

parts.note: from the Telegraph's own point of view, its possession is ours
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A judge challenges the paper's refusal to name a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle is in the Telegraph, so 'the Telegraph's' is the paper speaking: OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A journo is informal slang for a journalist, a writer for the press, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Not working, having left monastery?

definitions.meaning: a monk who has quit a religious order is jokingly out of it

explanation.definitionFit: A broken machine is unserviceable; a monk who departs no longer belongs to the religious community.

clue.text: Operatic heroine acted start of opera

parts.note: did means acted or performed

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of opera

explanation.surface: A singer played the heroine at the opening of the opera.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of Carthage is the title role in Purcell's Dido and Aeneas.

clue.text: Abuse working vet about one time having ram brought in

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters go round the rest
working signals that the letters of vet are put to work in a new order
brought in means the animal goes inside one and time

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an era is a period of time
a tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A vet at work swears at a ram that has been brought in for treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' makes VTE from VET, wrapped 'about' I-TUP-ERA. TUP is a dialect word for a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: To vituperate is to berate someone with harsh, insulting language, a verb matching abuse.

clue.text: Refuse to go uphill without prior experience

parts.note: bran is the husks left after milling, waste or refuse

indicators.note: uphill in a down clue means climbing upward, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: to wend is to go on one's way

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to climb the hill, being a complete novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fresh from the factory has never been used, so it has no history behind it.

clue.text: Very moved by weakness in worship

indicators.note: moved signals the letter for very shifts to a different place in the word

parts.note: enervation is a state of weakness or exhaustion

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply touched by frailty during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ENERVATION and move its V to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneration is deep reverence, the respect paid to something held sacred.

clue.text: Note taxmen blocking twelve as 'unsuitable for board'

indicators.note: blocking means the note and taxmen are put into the middle of twelve

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock
IR is the Inland Revenue, Britain's former tax authority

explanation.surface: A note says twelve tax inspectors are not fit to sit on a board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric labelled so needs no pressing, so it does not belong on an ironing board.

clue.text: Estimate the work to be done

definitions.meaning: a speculative guess, as in buying something on the chance
a specification setting out a job's requirements

explanation.definitionFit: Short for speculation, a rough guess; short for specification, the brief for a job.

clue.text: Filthy monster drilling tree

indicators.note: drilling means the monster bores into the tree

parts.note: a pine is a tree
an orc is a monster of folklore and Tolkien

explanation.surface: A disgusting beast bores into a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcine means pig-like, and pigs are proverbially dirty, so it can stand for grubby.

clue.text: Intended simple person to rise over church

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above the next piece
to rise in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a naif is an innocent or unsophisticated person
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A simpleton meant to get up above a church.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is one's betrothed, a man engaged to be married.

clue.text: Additional layer left in, in front of garment

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of garment

explanation.surface: An extra layer was left in at the front of a piece of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner fabric sewn inside a coat is an extra layer of material.

clue.text: Assert Collider finally working — here's a particle

parts.note: to posit is to assert

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of collider

parts.note: on means working or functioning

explanation.surface: A physicist claims that, now the collider is running at last, a particle has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: The antimatter twin of the electron is a subatomic particle with positive charge.

clue.text: Small area of ground Italy wasted? Not entirely

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: wasted is slang for killed, and slew is the past of slay

explanation.surface: A patch of Italian land has been laid waste, at least in part.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet or small island is a little area of land surrounded by water.

clue.text: Unknown political movements? They're unmentionable!

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
a front is a political movement or alliance

explanation.surface: Mysterious political groups are too shameful to name.
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are a British style of men's briefs; unmentionables is a coy word for underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is jokingly called unmentionables, and these briefs are such garments.

clue.text: Study coming to point, identifying bony material

parts.note: a den is a study or private room
a tine is a prong or point

explanation.surface: Research comes to a head, identifying a type of bony tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard calcified tissue under tooth enamel is a bone-like material.

clue.text: After this, you'd be unlucky to lose your footing

definitions.text: After this, you'd be unlucky to lose your footing

parts.words: After this, you'd be unlucky to lose your footing
parts.note: first-footing is the Scottish custom of the first visitor after midnight bringing luck, so missing it is unlucky

explanation.walkthrough: Footing suggests slipping over, but it is the Hogmanay first-footing tradition, where the first guest of the year brings luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The night of 31 December precedes the first-footing ritual that follows midnight.
